end.summary:
Discussed speed as distance ÷ time, using 120 m in 10 s = 12 m/s.
Distinguished speed from velocity by adding direction.
Explored displacement: same start and end point gives zero; different points give non-zero displacement.
Calculated average speed as total distance ÷ total time: 120 km ÷ 3 h = 40 km/h.
Acceleration from braking was introduced but not completed; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: They correctly calculated 12 m/s and 40 km/h and later explained that displacement is zero when the object returns to its starting point. The earlier displacement mix-up was clarified, but the acceleration formula for the braking question was not completed. At home, draw a path with labelled start and end points and ask Diya to identify distance, displacement, and direction.
